## Course resources

### Statistics cheat sheet

Use the [statistics cheat sheet](cheat-sheet.qmd) as a short reference for the IMS self-study and the quiz.

It covers observations, variables, variable types, population and sample, contingency tables, bar plots, scatterplots, mean, histograms, median, quartiles, and box plots.

Every chart on the cheat sheet comes from a worked example, so you can see what each display shows and what it hides.

### Introduction to Modern Statistics (2e)

@cetinkayarundel2024ims is a free online textbook with exercises. The [GitHub repository](https://github.com/openintrostat/ims/) holds the source files.

### All Data Are Local

@loukissas2019 is an open-access book from MIT Press.

## Optional learning resources

### MaDaLi² — Mannheim Data Literacy

@madali2 is bilingual German and English self-study material. No prior knowledge is required. Useful modules include data ethics, data collection, data management, analysis, interpretation, and publication.

### Data Carpentry — Social Sciences

@datacarpentry offers practical lessons on spreadsheet structure, data cleaning with OpenRefine, and data analysis workflows.

### Seeing Theory

@seeingtheory gives interactive visual explanations of probability and statistics. Use it for intuition and optional review.

## Data protection

### Swiss Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC)

@fdpic publishes the official legal information on Swiss data protection.

Before you use personal data, check two things. Check whether the data contain information about identifiable people. Check whether your planned use is lawful and appropriate.

The [literature](literature.qmd) page lists the full reference for every resource on this page.
